Kyle Miller said:

Is there a way for me to "jump to definition"

There's not a great way to do this right now from the "failed to synthesize" error. The typeclass instance synthesis system isn't able to answer "these are the instances you'd need to be able to synthesize this instance". It's frustrating, and you sometimes have to add in decidable instances (or use open scoped Classical) to see if that's the reason the instance can't be found.

Here's one possibility: Type this in

variable {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] (s t : Finset α)
#check s ∪ t

then hover over the union symbol in the infoview, and see that there's an instance argument that uses the word finset

image.png

Then, on a mac, command click on that to go to the definition.

This instance is written in an indirect way for some reason. It only gives the proof argument, letting the type of the proof fill in that it calculates the union with docs#Multiset.ndunion

image.png

Edit: this screenshot was supposed to include the hover, but it didn't make it in. It had the type of the underlined proof term.

Related to this and something that confused me while reading the documentation, the docs say Finset.instUnion but going to source gives this unnamed instance. Where does this naming come from if its not specified in the instance definition, also Finset.instUnionFinset and Finset.instInterFinset confused me because they don't exist when searching in mathlib docs and there's also Finset.instUnion and Finset.instInter already mentioned. Is this a mistake in the docs or some kind of convention?
Instance names are auto-generated if not explicitly named, you can see their names if you hover over the word instance in your editor

what about Finset.instUnionFinset mentioned in the docs?

This seems like a mistake, possibly because the naming algorithm changed between Lean 3 & Lean 4 (but I'm not sure).
I assume a PR fixing it would be welcome!

I think the docstring should avoid mentioning instance names, especially since comments like "Finset.instUnionFinset: Defines s ∪ t as the union of s and t" are redundant IMO. The existing "This file puts a lattice structure on finite sets" is clear enough.

well i made a pull request just fixing the typos.

There is a 'Main Declarations' heading mentioning them , which i think should be kept as a quick overview for anyone browsing.

What i do think is redundant is the following

### Operations on two or more finsets

* `Finset.instUnionFinset`: see "The lattice structure on subsets of finsets"
* `Finset.instInterFinset`: see "The lattice structure on subsets of finsets"

unless see "The lattice structure on subsets of finsets" is supposed to link somewhere...

It looks like it used to exist before #18610 in Data/Finset/Basic.lean, it referred to the paragraph that is now in ## Main declarations. That PR split the whole lattice part into a separate file, and I believe the reference should now be see the current file or see above, which is of course redundant.

I'm reading the mathlib documentation style and encountered the following

Implementation notes (description of important design decisions or interface features,
including use of type classes and
simp canonical form for new definitions)

The lattice aspect of finset requires DecidableEqtypeclass in almost everything , is adding an implementation notes heading appropriate here and do i present what i come up with here first before pushing a new commit? I am asking this because I'm new when it comes to contributing to mathlib

You can change what you want in the PR, reviewers will review it and tell you what they agree or disagree with.
As for implementation notes, it could be nice to mention decidable equality, e.g. "we require decidable equality to keep everything computable".
I wouldn't sweat the details though. You might like https://youtu.be/4gTZsshdaqg btw
